## K10 · K10-design — K10: design endpoint destruction without an all-thread scan

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 3

Decision references: 07cc10573acbc8403ea6b39cc8aa46a3, ceb5b9c90

Evidence: K10 design settled (no owner choice): not the reverse-index hatch; the fix batches destroy_endpoint's three per-endpoint all-thread scans into one bounded walk keyed on the endpoint's owner dying. R10 becomes one MAX_PROCESS_COUNT x MAX_THREADS walk + the subtree's own parked calls, not endpoints x threads. Design committed as ceb5b9c90 (budgets.md item 4); brief at .wash/local/K10-implementer.md.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `2d9f490fc75bd194a0db5266a120e8db` · 2026-09-30T09:50:40Z

> K10 (endpoint destruction no longer scans every thread) is now the active package - the escape hatch you flagged in K9-design ("a full handle reverse index... reopen here rather than widen").
> 
> GATE1's full-fill run found: destroy_endpoint (message.rs:1580) calls fail_all three times per endpoint, each driving find_thread (message.rs:426), which scans MAX_PROCESS_COUNT x MAX_THREADS. So R10 is O(owned endpoints x processes x threads): a full lease (~1460 endpoints, 9 leases/slot, rv64 seed 3) destroys at R10 p99 ~1,900,033 us and notice p99 ~1,169,004 us (18 samples) vs 30/40 ms. Bounded scaling confirms it: 20 endpoints 55,909 us, 150 endpoints 240,963 us. K9 removed the whole-object-frame scan; this per-endpoint all-thread scan is what remains, and the gate's designed full fill exposes it.
> 
> Design the fix: make an endpoint's destruction fail only the calls actually parked on that endpoint (a per-endpoint parked/open-call list, or the reverse index you described), so R10 is O(the dying subtree's own parked calls), not O(every thread). State the invariant, what the two fail_all paths become, and the rv32/128-slots cost-model consequence. Write the design on the owning page and cut .wash/local/K10-implementer.md (reading list, owned paths, traps). Confirm the owner's "no widened target, no weakened attacker" holds; flag any owner choice.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `a211047fe004f310dbe3bd6559af19ae` · 2026-09-30T09:57:23Z

> K10 design: settled from the pages; no owner choice. This is not the K9 reverse-index hatch — the bottleneck now is destroy_endpoint's three per-endpoint all-thread scans, not a handle index, so the fix is simpler and changes no layout.
> 
> Direction: batch the endpoint teardown's per-endpoint scans into one bounded thread walk per destruction.
> - destroy_endpoint (message.rs:1580) runs two fail_all (find_thread over MAX_PROCESS_COUNT × MAX_THREADS) plus a F_NOTICE loop plus endpoint_dying (≤64) — each per endpoint, so R10 is endpoints × threads.
> - They move into one fail_all in budgets_dying, keyed on "the endpoint's owner is dying" (budget_at(endpoint.owner).dying, one frame read), merging with the existing stamp pass; F_NOTICE clear and exit-notice drop join the same pass. destroy_endpoint then only frees the frame (already deferred by K9's one sweep).
> 
> So R10 becomes O(dying subtree's endpoints to free + one bounded walk + its own parked calls), not O(endpoints × threads). The walk is the same MAX_PROCESS_COUNT × MAX_THREADS R2 already makes to pick a sender.
> 
> Invariant: R10 step 4 unchanged — each waiter fails exactly once with Dead, receivers first, nothing names a freed frame (I1/I2), deferred frame free composes with the one handle sweep.
> 
> Cost-model/128-slots: none — no new words, HANDLES_PER_PAGE untouched, no reverse index; the walk is already bounded. rv32 identical.
> 
> Owner guard holds: targets stay 30/40/105/135; the full fill (~1460) stays hostile. No owner choice.
> 
> Design on docs/kernel/budgets.md residual risks (item 4). Brief at .wash/local/K10-implementer.md.
